messages:
alex: quick question \/ please advise 30 my dad needs a 7-day outpatient PICC line and daily home infusion (antibiotic). How can I estimate what we'll owe vs what insurer pays under Redwood Choice PPO? Also will a screenshot of the e-card and the provider's invoice be enough for claims?

sara (People Ops): hey alex  quick overview: for home infusion you usually need pre-certification (sometimes called prior auth or pre-authorization). Coverage and member cost depend on whether the provider is in-network, whether the service is medically necessary, and if the visit triggers deductible or copay. For Redwood Choice PPO: infusion nursing often applies to coinsurance after deductible for hospital-level services, but exact share varies by CPT/HCPCS codes.

alex: ah ok. any quick place to check in-network status and negotiated rates?

sara (People Ops): fastest is benefits.redwood.com -> Find a Provider (search by agency name or NPI). For negotiated amounts we don't publish rates publicly; to estimate OOP, you can: 1) confirm in-network status, 2) ask vendor for an itemized estimate with CPT/HCPCS codes, 3) use insurer's member cost estimator or call member services and provide the CPT codes to get a benefits estimate.

toni: vendor tip  if the agency refuses direct-bill, ask them to bill with place-of-service = home and include the auth number on claim. Also request an itemized invoice marked "patient responsibility" before you pay.

alex: what about documentation to submit with prior auth and claims? anything they commonly forget?

sara (People Ops): yes - common misses: signed physician order with start/stop dates, clinical progress note justifying home care vs facility, plan of care (frequency, supplies, med dosing), and any infusion nursing conversion notes. For claims, include auth number, NPI, taxonomy, and the member/group ID. If they used a different billing name, include the DBA.

benefits-bot: automated reminder  Prior auth turnaround: standard 3-5 business days. Expedited reviews possible if medically urgent (72h). Keep copies of auth letter or member services confirmation. If you get a phone auth, note the rep name and reference number.

alex: will a screenshot of the digital ID be OK for the agency to bill? or do they need a PDF or physical card?

sara (People Ops): screenshot is usually fine as proof of coverage if it clearly shows member ID and group number. If provider asks for additional verification, they can call the insurer's provider line and verify using the member ID and DOB. Try to get them to confirm they will accept direct-billing to avoid paying upfront.

alex: any sample text I can send the agency to start auth and ask for estimate?

sara (People Ops): yep - shorter template below, feel free to edit.

```
Subject: Prior Auth Request and Estimate Needed  [Member: Alex Dad, DOB: MM/DD/YYYY]

Hi [Agency],

Please submit a prior authorization for home infusion nursing and PICC care for [Member Name] (Member ID: [########], Group: [######]). Service: PICC insertion follow-up + daily infusion x7. Attached: signed physician order, plan of care, and medication details (drug, dose, route, frequency). Please provide: 1) authorization/pre-cert number, 2) itemized estimate with CPT/HCPCS and expected patient responsibility (deductible/coinsurance estimate), and 3) confirmation whether you will direct-bill the insurer or require patient payment. If you are out-of-network, please include NPI and billing entity name. Send approvals and estimate to [alex@email.com].

Thanks,
Alex
```

toni: fwiw take a screenshot of any phone confirmation and upload to insurer portal. If claim denies later for lack of auth, call provider relations; they sometimes retro-authorize when documentation is supplied quickly.

sara (People Ops): if you hit a denial or the agency wants you to pay up front, escalate to people-ops@redwood.com with the denial EOB and vendor invoice and we can help coordinate an appeal or a bill direct-bill push. Good luck  and let us know if you want us to confirm network status (you can DM the agency name or NPI).
